scope: Read renderer code, then parent-authorized targeted auxiliary-cache and allocation guards. No runtime benchmark, browser, build or server.

gpuBehavior.coarsePages: Every page retains a low mip chain; can coarsen as far as128px in the current2048/5mip chain.
gpuBehavior.fineCells: Visible cells and nearby cells stream into fixed GPU slots, with LRU eviction; offscreen mip0 pages are not globally resident.
gpuBehavior.compressedProductionDiscovery: scripts/assets/atlas-ktx2.mjs bundles actual ATLAS_PAGES, so object-eight imports are included automatically. Development uses RGBA WebP fallback.

scenarios.note: These are formula estimates, not measured process memory. Existing atlas pages/older runtime versions add to this count.

implementedBounds.startupPicking: Two concurrent page fetch/decode/readbacks; bit-packed opacity preserves exact threshold and page indices. ImageBitmap closed and canvas backing explicitly zeroed.
implementedBounds.previewImages: Two-page LRU for full2048px2D ghost sources, about32MiB raw pixels. Eviction removes src; Game.destroy clears retained elements. Browser-managed caches are separate.
implementedBounds.thumbnails: IntersectionObserver gates source/mip1 requests to viewport-visible cards; two concurrent source-to-thumbnail tasks. Small finished thumbnails remain reusable.
implementedBounds.pickingFailure: Missing alpha data cannot substitute an opaque rectangle; those unavailable masks do not intercept clicks.
implementedBounds.arrayLimit: AtlasGL rejects pages>actualMAX_ARRAY_TEXTURE_LAYERS before allocating textures/decoding. Source workers disposed. Does not split arrays.
implementedBounds.minimumCoarseBudget: Rejects a minimum coarse set above atlas byte budget before allocation. Error directs approved shared-page packing.
implementedBounds.startupRejection: Atlas rejection is attached immediately, stops subsequent alpha jobs and propagates as a real init failure; no invalid blank-page fallback.

remainingLimits: One low-mip array still has one layer per catalogue page. Unsupported catalogues now fail clearly instead of allocating invalid textures.

Per-subject/version2048pages still waste space and increase startup I/O, low mip residency and picking bits. Shared batch packing at calibrated display density is still needed for catalogue-wide imports.

Existing streamed-level decode cache keeps two idle levels in the game; referenced/in-flight levels and browser decode working sets can temporarily exceed that. These changes do not claim a strict total process-RAM ceiling.
No GPU maximum or actual combined RAM usage was measured on this PC. The background LLM was not touched.
nextSmallestPipelineWork: Pack multiple approved native subjects into shared immutable atlas pages, preserving native originals/provenance/IDs; preserve full native masters outside GPU assets and target existing0.6atlas-pixel/display-pixel packing convention where appropriate. Keep explicit layer/coarse-budget preflight guard; implement array banks only if efficiently packed actual data still exceeds device limits.
